key_insight: A spectrally regularized latent compression stage dramatically improves latent flow matching for turbulence by preserving dissipation-range amplitudes that MSE-trained VAEs suppress.
engineering_relevance: This yields far better sample fidelity at low inference cost, making generative turbulence models more practical for reduced-order simulation and data-driven flow synthesis.
method: Replace an MSE-trained VAE with a spectrally regularized, zone-weighted log-spectral encoder-decoder.
Train latent flow matching on the improved latent space for unconditional turbulence generation.
Use encoder-decoder swap and support-amplitude analyses to isolate where spectral fidelity gains originate.
evidence_signal: On a 256^2 DNS dataset at Re_f ≈ 2250, deep-dissipation retained spectral power improved from 25% to 94% in reconstruction and from 20% to 79% in generation, with DD bias improving to -0.117 at 20 function evaluations.
watch_item: The abstract notes a residual magnitude gap in S_3, suggesting phase-coherent triadic structure is still imperfect and may limit full physical realism.
paper_title: Spectrally Regularized Latent Flow Matching for Turbulence Generation
